home.heroLead: SMS one-time codes for your backend.
home.heroBody: Your server calls the HTTP API — the gateway generates a code and sends it to the user. There is no signup on this site: an operator issues the API key and shows it once.
home.howLeadBefore: Three steps on the client side. A request example is in the
home.step1Body: An operator creates an account and gives you an API key of the form otp_…. Calls without a key are rejected.
home.step2Body: From your server, send POST /api/send-otp with the x-api-key header and a { "phone" } body. The gateway generates the code; SMS text: Your {brandName} code: {code}. The response includes code.
home.step3Body: Compare the code the user entered with code from the response. SMS quota is per account; when it runs out the API returns 429 — the operator will top up the limit.
home.keyHeading: How to get an API key
home.keyLead: You cannot create a key on this site. An operator issues it.
home.keyStep1NoChannels: You request access from the operator who issues accounts.
home.keyStep2: The operator creates an account: SMS quota, brand name, OTP length 4–8.
home.keyStep3After: . Store it only on the server (environment variable or a secret store).
home.keyStep4: If the key is lost, the operator issues a new one; the old key stops working.
home.security1: Store the key on the server only. Do not call the API from a mobile app or web client.
home.security2: Do not commit the key to git, pass it in the query string, or embed it in client apps.
home.security4: Do not reuse one key across products if the operator issued separate accounts.
home.contactLeadWithChannels: To get an API key, write to us.
home.contactLeadNoChannels: To get an API key, contact the operator who issues accounts.
home.ctaBody: Ready to call POST /api/send-otp from your server? Full request and response examples are in the documentation.

docs.intro: Guide to the Abat OTP HTTP channel: how to store an operator-issued key and how to call POST /api/send-otp from your backend. Calls must be server-to-server. Status queued means the gateway accepted the message into the queue, not that the SMS was delivered.
docs.keyIntroBefore: An operator issues your key. There is no self-service signup: arrange access
docs.keyOnce: The raw key is shown once. Store it on the server immediately (secret store or backend environment variables), not in a repository and not in a client app. Format: otp_YOUR_API_KEY (prefix otp_). If the key is lost, the operator will reissue it; the previous key stops working.
docs.connectHttps: Call the API only from your server over HTTPS. Do not put the key in a browser, mobile app, or query string.
docs.connectBase: The base URL is the same origin as this page, or the HTTPS host your operator named. Example path: https://YOUR_DOMAIN/api/send-otp. In production it may look like https://sms.elkitap.com/api/send-otp — that is a host illustration, not open signup.
docs.connectHeaders: Every request: Content-Type: application/json and the x-api-key header with the operator-issued key.
docs.sendIntro: The request body contains only the phone number. A message field, if sent, is ignored: the gateway builds the SMS text as Your {brandName} code: {code}.
docs.phoneRule: After trim, phone must match ^\+?\d{8,16}$ (optional +, then 8–16 digits).
docs.queuedExplain: queued means the gateway accepted the message into the queue; it is not a delivery receipt. The operator sets code length for your account (4 to 8 digits). SMS quota is charged when the message is queued, not when it reaches the handset.
docs.errQueueFull: Service busy; quota is not charged
docs.exampleLead: Node.js (fetch). Call only from your backend:
docs.sec1: Store the key on the server only. Do not send it to the frontend or put it in the query string.
docs.sec2: If the key leaks, ask the operator to reissue it.
docs.sec3: Use separate keys per environment (dev / staging / prod) if the operator issued them.
docs.sec6: 503 — retry later; quota is not charged for this response.
docs.sec7: The returned code is a secret for verification on your side. Do not log it in production.
